description:
Take a screenshot of whichever target `device` resolves to: iOS simulator, USB-attached iPhone/iPad, Android device/emulator, or chromium (Electron / Chrome) window. Returns the image plus a screen-state summary: active route, overlay-grouped tappable elements (pressables behind an open sheet/modal excluded), component names as JSX tags, labels, testIDs and frames in ready-to-tap pixel coordinates. Use component names for inspect_component/find_components.
PURPOSE: The capture tool for every platform. See what the user sees AND get tap-ready pressables in one call.
WHEN TO USE: Visual verification, before/after comparison, or the starting point for tapping by coordinates.
WORKFLOW: screenshot -> pick a pressable -> tap(text=...) if exact and unique, else tap(x, y) -> screenshot to verify.
COORDINATES: image pixels are the coordinates tap(x, y) takes, on every platform. Never scale them yourself.
PHYSICAL iOS: pass the UDID or name from list_devices. Capture only: no pressables, no tap/swipe/input_text.
LIMITATIONS: a hidden or minimised chromium window cannot be captured: the call fails at once and says so.
GOOD: screenshot(); screenshot({ device: "FluentTalk" })
BAD: a made-up device name or UDID, run list_devices first.
SOURCE: inspect_at_point(x, y) maps a pixel to the file and line that renders it.

device.description: Target: a connected app name (get_apps), or a simulator/emulator name, UDID or adb serial. Omit for the default target.

outputPath.description: Optional path to also save the image to.

name: screenshot
